Regarding the readability of the provided text ("The cat sat on the mat. It was a sunny day, and the birds were singing. There was a gentle breeze that played with the leaves of the trees."), here is an evaluation using standard formulas:

**1. Flesch Reading Ease (FRE)**
*   **Formula:** $206.835 - 1.015 \times (\text{total words} / \text{total sentences}) - 84.6 \times (\text{total syllables} / \text{total words})$
*   **Analysis:**
    *   Total Words: 33
    *   Total Sentences: 3
    *   Average Words per Sentence: 11
    *   Total Syllables: 42
    *   Average Syllables per Word: $42 / 33 \approx 1.27$
    *   Calculation: $206.835 - 1.015(11) - 84.6(1.27) \approx 206.835 - 11.165 - 107.442 \approx 88.2$
*   **Score:** ~88.2
*   **Interpretation:** Very Easy. This text is easily understood by an average 11-year-old student. It is suitable for general audiences and children.

**2. Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level (FKGL)**
*   **Formula:** $0.39 \times (\text{total words} / \text{total sentences}) + 11.8 \times (\text{total syllables} / \text{total words}) - 15.59$
*   **Calculation:** $0.39(11) + 11.8(1.27) - 15.59 \approx 4.29 + 14.986 - 15.59 \approx 3.69$
*   **Score:** ~3.7
*   **Interpretation:** This text corresponds to a U.S. 3rd or 4th-grade reading level.

**Summary:**
The text is highly readable,
